saints.name: St. Peter Damian
saints.title: Bishop and Doctor of the Church
saints.shortBlurb: A hermit-monk of stern reform drawn against his will to be a cardinal-bishop, whose pen scourged the vices of a troubled age…
biography: Born at Ravenna about 1007 and orphaned young, Peter was starved and set to swineherding by one brother until another, Damian, the archpriest of Ravenna, had him educated; in gratitude he took his brother's name. After brilliant studies at Faenza and Parma he taught rhetoric, then about 1035 withdrew to the hermitage of Fonte Avellana, becoming its prior in 1043.

From his cloister he thundered against the simony and incontinence of the clergy, addressing his searing Liber Gomorrhianus to Pope Leo IX about 1050. In 1057 Pope Stephen IX forced on him the cardinal-bishopric of Ostia; as legate he reformed the church of Milan in 1059, and in 1069 he dissuaded the emperor Henry IV from repudiating his wife Bertha.

Released at last from his see, he died on the road at Faenza on 22 February 1072, returning from a mission of reconciliation to Ravenna, and was venerated without any formal canonization. Dante set him in the heaven of Saturn, and in 1828 Pope Leo XII declared him a Doctor of the Church.
saints.knownFor: His writings and his zeal for the eleventh-century reform of the Church.

canonization.canonized: Venerated from antiquity; declared a Doctor of the Church in 1828 by Pope Leo XII

sources.text: Butler, Lives of the Saints (1866 ed.), 23 February
